name: Images of Text (No Exception)
explanation: This is the stricter, AAA-level version of SC 1.4.5 Images of Text. At the AA level, an image of text is allowed if a particular visual presentation is 'essential,' meaning the specific look can't be reproduced with real text and CSS. This criterion removes that exception entirely. The only image of text still permitted is a logo or brand name, where the image itself is the thing being identified. Everything else — headings, pull quotes, decorative typographic treatments — must be real text, even if the exact visual effect can't be perfectly recreated. In practice this means teams must get as close as possible using a real web font and CSS, and accept that a small amount of visual fidelity may be sacrificed in exchange for text that is genuinely resizable and machine-readable.
whoItAffects: People with low vision who rely on browser zoom or OS-level text scaling get no benefit from an image, no matter how 'necessary' its designer felt the visual treatment was. The AA essential-presentation exception offered them nothing in practice, which is exactly why AAA removes it. People using reading and translation tools can't process words baked into pixels, so a decorative image of text silently drops out of translation or read-aloud entirely, even when it was 'unavoidable' at AA. Screen reader users are left entirely dependent on whatever alt text was authored, with no way to inspect the actual typography or emphasis the sighted design conveys. Organizations adopting AAA, often government or health services aiming for the highest conformance level, commit to prioritizing this universal access over preserving a specific decorative effect.

codeExample.good: Handwritten with Heart: Our 2026 Community Campaign

howToTest: First apply the SC 1.4.5 test: zoom to 200% and look for blurring or pixelation, and try to select the text. Then, for any image of text you find, ask whether it's a logo or brand name. If so, it's still fine at AAA. If it's not a logo, it fails this criterion regardless of any justification about the visual presentation being 'essential' — at AAA, that justification no longer applies. The only question that matters here is: is it a logo, yes or no?

check.question: A page uses a PNG image for a section heading because the designer used a highly customized letter-spacing and outline effect that genuinely cannot be reproduced with CSS or any available web font. It is not a logo. Does this satisfy SC 1.4.9 Images of Text (No Exception)?
choices: Yes, because the visual presentation is essential and unreproducible, which excuses it
No, because SC 1.4.9 removes the essential-presentation exception that exists at AA — only logos are exempt
Yes, as long as the image has descriptive alt text
No, but only because the image file is a PNG rather than an SVG
